html:
SMTO-UI-0050 — That shortcut can't be used to open the Command Palette

GUID: 6e043c08-5cc9-5732-bdf6-a01404b757a8
Slug: palette-hotkey-conflict
Domain: UI · Subsystem: ui

What happened

  • The shortcut you typed isn't allowed, either because it isn't written the right way or because your browser or SMTO already uses it. Your old shortcut still works.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the Command Palette, open Invocation settings and type a shortcut in In-app shortcut as Control or Meta, a plus sign, then one letter, for example Control+K. The shortcut must use Control or Meta (the Command key on a Mac) plus a single letter.
  2. If you want a different letter, use K, G or M, or add Alt, for example Control+Alt+P. Then select Save for this tab. Most other letters, such as Control+N or Control+T, already belong to your browser or to SMTO.
  3. If the saved shortcut still doesn't open the palette, choose another one or use the Command palette button. Your computer may grab some key combinations before the browser sees them.

What success looks like

  • The message under the settings says the shortcut was saved, and pressing it opens the Command Palette.

If it still fails

  • Use the Command palette button instead, and send the copied error details to the person who manages SMTO. Don't turn on Input Monitoring or a keyboard hook to make a shortcut work.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The in-app Command Palette shortcut was rejected because it is not Control/Meta plus one letter (optional Alt/Shift) or it matches a reserved browser or app shortcut.

What this means

  • Palette shortcut normalization rejects an unsupported key/modifier shape or a known reserved shortcut. The shown control rejects this local action before its dependent submission. Earlier requests and saved state are unaffected by this validation result; server-side authority remains authoritative.

Why this can happen

  • Palette shortcut normalization rejects an unsupported key/modifier shape or a known reserved shortcut.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the proposed binding with supported modifiers and reserved combinations; OS interception is separate.

How to fix it

  • normalizeShortcut() in agent_ui/command_palette.js accepts modifier+letter chords that include Control or Meta, with no duplicate modifiers; without Alt, the letters n t w l r p f h q o s a c v x z y b j d u i e are reserved. Use e.g. Control+K, Control+G, Control+M or any Control/Meta+Alt+letter; the value is stored per tab as palette_shortcut in the UI session state.
  • Use Control or Meta plus a letter, optionally Alt/Shift. Choose an unused binding such as Control+K. If the OS intercepts it, use another binding or the palette button.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the invocation configuration before trying again.

How to verify the fix

  • A valid saved binding opens the palette while the page is focused.

What not to do

  • Do not enable Input Monitoring or a keyboard hook to invoke the palette.

Technical notes

  • The shown control rejects this local action before its dependent submission. Earlier requests and saved state are unaffected by this validation result; server-side authority remains authoritative.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
